rationale: Intentional public read path for the signed-out marketing regulatory-updates page, mirroring public.verify_certificate. list_regulatory_updates is SECURITY DEFINER with a fixed status='published' filter and search_path pinned to 'public', so anon callers can only read already-published feed rows -- draft/archived content and the base table stay unreachable (no anon table grant).

Intentional public walk-up path for /report-safety posters and QR codes. SECURITY DEFINER with search_path pinned empty; accepts only an opaque facility token (or a legacy UUID) and returns facilityId/name -- never a facility directory. Since 20260905130000 the safety_report_token comes back ONLY to a caller who already presented it: the legacy UUID branch returns null for it, because facility UUIDs appear in URLs throughout the product and handing the current token to anyone holding one made rotation meaningless. Mirrors public.verify_certificate: anon can execute the resolver, base table has no anon grant.

Re-grant of the pre-existing public certificate-verification path, unchanged in intent. verify_certificate had to be dropped and recreated to widen its RETURNS TABLE (course code, version label, credential number, examination score, training provider and credential), and a dropped function takes its grants with it. It stays SECURITY DEFINER with search_path pinned to 'public' and is still keyed on the certificate's opaque random slug, returning only what the printed certificate already states; the certificates table itself has no anon grant.

Re-grant of the same pre-existing public certificate-verification path allowlisted for 20260830120000, unchanged in intent and in exposure. verify_certificate is replaced here only to read the provider name and credential snapshotted onto the certificate at issuance instead of joining the mutable course_provider_profiles row, so an edit to that profile can no longer restate what an already-issued certificate claims. CREATE OR REPLACE preserves grants, but the statement is re-issued alongside the REVOKE so the function's access is stated in full at the point it is defined rather than inherited silently. Same signature, same columns, same SECURITY DEFINER with search_path pinned to 'public', and lookup still requires the unguessable per-certificate slug; no table grant to anon is added.

Re-grant of the pre-existing public certificate-verification path, NARROWED rather than widened. verify_certificate had to be dropped and recreated to remove final_exam_score from its RETURNS TABLE (BACKLOG.md I16: the slug is a bearer token that travels in emails and printed PDFs, and a verifier needs to know the credential is real, not what the learner scored), and a drop takes the grant with it. Still SECURITY DEFINER with search_path pinned empty, still keyed on a single opaque slug, and it returns strictly less than before; the certificates table has no anon grant.

The gate in front of the seventeen anonymous guest and resident-portal RPCs, which are themselves anon-executable by design (tokenised link, no account). It has to be callable by the same role they are, because each one calls it as its first statement. It is the narrowest anon grant in the schema: RETURNS VOID, so it hands the caller no data at all -- its only outcomes are to return, or to raise. What it does is count the caller's requests per minute, record a token that resolved to nothing (hashed, in app_private, unreadable from this surface), and refuse a suspended organization's outstanding links. SECURITY DEFINER with search_path pinned empty because it writes app_private counters that anon cannot reach, and it deliberately allows a first unknown token through so it adds no oracle about which tokens exist. BACKLOG.md I16.
